summary: LDAP is operational on node1 for dc=branch,dc=test. Node2 finds both staged users remotely. Anonymous writes are denied, authenticated administrator updates succeed, and all functionality persisted through sequential node restarts. RHEL 10.0 and the existing kernel remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Installed RHEL-compatible 389 Directory Server on node1 and LDAP client utilities on both nodes.
Created and enabled the branch directory instance on port 389.
Generated the administrator credential on node1 and protected it with root-only permissions.
Imported alex and sam with their original names and mail addresses.
Allowed anonymous read/search access to public directory attributes while retaining authenticated-only writes.
Verified authenticated administration and rejected anonymous writes.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially, confirming changed boot identities and full recovery after each.

evidence.summary: Node1 is active, enabled, listening on port 389, and contains alex@branch.test and sam@branch.test with the supplied identities.

evidence.requirement: Node2 can search the people subtree
evidence.summary: Remote searches from node2 returned both users before and after restarts.
Directory Manager authenticated, applied a test update, and cleanly reverted it.
Anonymous modifications returned LDAP error 50, and direct searches confirmed no unauthorized data persisted, including after restarts.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel retained
evidence.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64.
Healthy baseline captured; reboot acknowledged; boot ID changed from 03408ac4… to 8b1e1eca…; service, listener, data, and remote access recovered.
Healthy baseline captured; reboot acknowledged; boot ID changed from 646e5f74… to 1c9abbb6…; LDAP client and remote directory search recovered.
